feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Here's why an Arizona medical examiner is working to track heat-related deaths
entry.summary: No one across the U.S. is consistently tracking climate-fueled deaths. One medical examiner has a new protocol on heat-deaths.

entry.title: House holds billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress over Epstein investigation
entry.summary: Billionaire investor Leon Black refused to appear before the committee investigating convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein for a deposition. Now it's up to the Department of Justice whether to pursue criminal charges.

entry.title: Volunteers help make mountain trails accessible for people with disabilities
entry.summary: It takes a group of dedicated volunteers to make sure mountain trails are wide enough so everyone can have fun.

entry.title: Cash aid can lead to improved financial circumstance, but can also increase conflict
entry.summary: In Liberia, the government gave cash transfers to couples to see if it would help solve problems that arise when partners disagree about how to manage money.

entry.title: A look at the secretive unit inside Department of Homeland Security
entry.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly talks with the reporter of a story that shows how the Department of Homeland Security is feeding information to local police as part of DHS' Predictive Intelligence Unit.

entry.title: What the Fed rate hike means for pocketbooks and politics
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates has broader political and economic implications, with affordability top of mind for voters ahead of the midterms.

entry.title: What Argentina gets right about youth soccer — and what the U.S. gets wrong
entry.summary: Argentina has produced some of the world's greatest soccer players. Could its youth system offer lessons for the United States?

entry.title: The 'burnerverse' exploiting young women in college
entry.summary: Wired reporter EJ Dickson speaks with NPR's Juana Summers about an online community that targets and harasses young women with their own nonconsensual, sexually explicit images.

entry.title: Fed raises interest rates for first time in more than three years
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates today Wednesday the first time in more than three years. The central bank is trying to curb stubborn inflation, which was rekindled by the war with Iran.

entry.title: Could genetically modified trees protect Florida's citrus industry?
entry.summary: Gene technology is giving hope to citrus farmers in Florida who are fighting greening disease, which has been killing their trees for two decades.
